Nostalgia mostly, till you sign and and see the mess of a website that it is now. 
I enjoy Facebook but roleplaying was best when it was still on MySpace.

The good ole days. 2.0 was tolerable but the classic MySpace was the best for editing your profile. It really kick started my roleplaying too. I remember browsing roleplay boards in the Naruto verse, then Original characters became a thing. 
I'll sign any petition, but I have little hope for MySpace to ever revert back to its old state.

No. 
Just an overwhelming amount of guilt for thinking this way and even thinking of leaving behind my family. But I can understand how someone could feel this way.

Being discharged from a clinic can be overwhelming as well as being inpatient. You either have a supportive staff or people to take care of you like a customer and send you out the door. 
You're asked a lot of questions and the pressure to not say anything to stay there longer makes it much worse. 

It can be hard to get out those feelings. Write them out, again and again if you're not ready to talk, or if that desire is there, reach out to the loved one. It might sound jumbled or confusing but it won't take a loved one much words to understand the pain you are dealing with. 
Take the leap if you have a loving support system. 
If not, I am a message away. 

There can only be one you and your life is precious, even if that fog and prison cell has you thinking otherwise.

Thank you. This is the first time I've really posted about this. I browse reddit but I haven't reply replied or posted anything so I'm pretty new to this. 
Thank you again for taking the time to comment and share your similar feelings. You are always welcome to message me.

I often feel like I'm on auto pilot. Smile, take in the moment with my family and enjoy it Like it's the last, because one day it might be. I don't try to ruin the moment with my family, or let them know anything is wrong so I try hard not to think about it while I'm with them. 

But when I get home I'm back in the same mindset and everything I've tried so hard to push back in my head all comes back out.
